And that starts at the ward level, gradually moving up to the local government and then the state levels.
But it is also at this stage that the public loses access to the entire electoral process.
The uploading of election results collated at the ward level to the Result Viewing Portal would have made 2027 the most transparent election in the country’s history.
But according to INEC, it would not electronically transmit and publish results from the ward, local government and state collation levels on its IReV portal.
There are at least 176,846 polling units and 8,809 wards designated for 2027. No one can keep up with results from all the polling units, but uploading ward and local government results would be a real game-changer.
But INEC, it seems, still wants total control over the process of collating results. This is another missed opportunity to regain public trust, leaving voters blind when it matters most .
